_comment: AGENT-EDITABLE and DORMANT. core/screen_value.py reads this and nothing else does.
Nothing in CYCLE.md, core/screen.py prepare or core/screen.py collect calls it, so an
edit here changes no live cycle. Same contract as strategy/screener-strata.json and
strategy/screener-filters.json: the code clamps every value into its own bounds, says
so loudly on stderr, and falls back to its built-in defaults if this file is missing or
malformed. A broken tuning file degrades the ranking, it never stops it.
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. The research tier is the scarce resource: about 950 markets
researched over 258 cycles for 654 forecasts. Escalation ranks by divergence, which the
2026-09-04 evaluator showed is in effect 'the markets priced nearest 50/50'. This file
holds the two things a prior over research edge needs and that a formula cannot invent:
which FAMILY a market belongs to, read off its title and slug without a model, and where
the BANDS fall on the numeric features. The fitting itself stays in core/screen_value.py
- the prior is estimated from journal/forecasts.jsonl, never written here by hand.
families: ordered rules, FIRST MATCH WINS, evaluated top to bottom. Each rule names a
family and one case-insensitive Python regex; `on` says whether the regex is matched
against the market question ('title') or the market slug ('slug'). A regex that fails
to compile is skipped loudly and the rest still apply. A rule naming a family outside
the fixed nine is dropped loudly - the family set is code, because the prior table's
shape has to be stable across an edit here. Anything that matches no rule is 'other'.
Order matters and is doing real work: the line-constructed rules run BEFORE the
moneyline rules, because 'Spread: Manchester City FC (-1.5)' is both a spread and a
soccer match and the spread is what makes its price uninformative.
Measured 2026-09-08 on the 542 settled non-superseded forecast rows: this mapper
agrees with the agent's own 56 free-text category labels on 95.6% of rows (518/542),
collapsed to the same nine families. Per family the rate is 1.000 on econ print,
entertainment, weather and crypto, 0.975 on sports line, 0.950 on sports moneyline,
0.912 on ai and tech, 0.981 on other, and 0.775 on politics. Most of the 24 residual
rows are the AGENT label being loose, not the mapper: nine rows labelled
'soccer-moneyline' or 'nfl-preseason' whose titles read 'Spread: ...' or 'O/U 34.5',
and two 'mlb-spreads' rows whose title and slug carry no line at all. The rest is the
agent's 'news' label, a grab bag of player transfers, net worth brackets and Middle
East geopolitics that no title rule can reproduce - which is itself the argument for
a fixed family set over 56 free-text labels the agent invents cycle by cycle.
price_band_edges: the market price at record time, in [0, 1], strictly increasing, 2 to
8 interior edges. Bands are [0, e0), [e0, e1), ... [en, 1]. The default cut is the one
the 2026-09-08 analysis asked for, plus the two tails the objective's five bands leave
out - a price under 0.05 or over 0.95 is a different animal from one at 0.10.
hours_to_resolution_edges: hours from the record timestamp to end_date, strictly
increasing positive numbers, 2 to 8 edges. A row recorded AFTER its own end_date (25h
at worst here, from a late settle) lands in the first band.
market_age_hours_edges: hours from the market's FIRST appearance in
journal/screener.jsonl to the record timestamp - the only market-age proxy this repo
can compute offline. It exists for 239 of 542 settled rows, and is NEGATIVE on 35 of
those (researched before the screener ever saw the market, because the screener
journal starts 2026-08-25). A negative age is not a young market, it is a missing
observation, so those rows score as unbanded rather than as the youngest band.
NOT HERE, deliberately: liquidity and 24h volume bands. Those numbers exist at record
time only inside reports/screener-work/<stamp>/batch-NN.json, and only 103 of the 542
settled rows fall in one of the 16 collect runs kept locally. That is too thin to fit a
band on, so the prior does not read them. If the briefs are ever retained for every run,
this is where the bands would go.

families.note: The screener-filters.json HARD RULE shape, as a family rather than a drop. A cover probability is set near 0.50 by construction.
The league-prefixed slug says the line explicitly. Anchored on a league prefix on purpose: an unanchored '-total-' also matches 'will-the-total-domestic-gross-for-spider-man'.
Standing no-bet category in the playbook; screener-filters.json already drops the daily bracket shape from the screen.
A scheduled, named official print. 'bank of' and 'official cash rate' carry the rate decisions, which are the same shape.
